info.title: Heliyos API
info.description: The REST API for Heliyos, the AI operating system for revenue. Every request is scoped to the workspace that owns the API key. Responses are JSON in a `{ meta, data }` envelope; errors use `{ message, error: { code, message, details } }`.

tags.name: Workspace
tags.description: The workspace your API key belongs to, and the log of credits it has used. Every other call in this API is scoped to this workspace.

tags.name: Schemas
tags.description: Objects are your record types: companies, people, deal pipelines and any custom objects you add. Each object has fields, and a field's type decides what its records can hold.

tags.name: Records
tags.description: Records are the rows of an object (base schema): companies, people, deals and custom objects. A record holds field values keyed by the object's field keys and links to other records.

tags.name: Timeline
tags.description: The AI-written timeline of a company, person or deal: summary entries Heliyos writes on a schedule. For the exact change history see Activities, and for emails and meetings see Interactions.

tags.name: Activities
tags.description: The change history of records and tasks: who created, changed or deleted what, and when. People, workers and the system each appear as the actor on the changes they make.

tags.name: Interactions
tags.description: Email threads and meetings synced from connected mailboxes and calendars, linked to the people and companies they involve.

tags.name: Notes
tags.description: Free-text notes, optionally linked to records, tasks and interactions. Notes show up on the timeline of every record they are linked to, and workers read them as customer memory.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description: Work items for people and workers, optionally linked to records. A task can be assigned to people, to workers, or both, and workers can be started on it directly.

tags.name: Workers and runs
tags.description: Workers are the AI teammates of your workspace (the API calls them agents). Define what each one does and what starts it, ask Heliyos to do work, and follow every run, its steps and the reviews it waits on.

tags.name: Reviews
tags.description: Reviews keep the team in control of consequential work. When a worker wants to send an email, change a deal, book a meeting, act in a connected app or needs a person's answer, the action waits as a review until someone approves or rejects it.

tags.name: Scouts
tags.description: Scouts watch companies and the web for events such as funding rounds, product launches, leadership changes or press coverage, and record each finding as a signal. A workspace Scout defines what to look for; company Scouts are its copies running on individual companies.

tags.name: Signals
tags.description: Signals are what Scouts find: one event, such as a funding round or a new executive, with a summary, its sources and the company it is about. New signals are unread until you mark them read.

tags.name: Watchlist
tags.description: The watchlist is the set of companies your workers monitor. Each watched company uses one Watcher from your plan: the workers keep it enriched, pull in its emails and meetings, and run Scouts on it.

tags.name: Knowledge base
tags.description: What your workers know about the business: the business context, four fixed texts (products, pain points, value proposition, qualification criteria) and any custom entries your team adds. Workers read it on their next run. Files your workers read live under Files, with kind `knowledge_base`.

tags.name: Files
tags.description: Knowledge base files that workers read, and files attached to records, tasks and other resources. The API calls them attachments. Uploading takes three calls: get an upload URL, send the bytes to it, then create the file.

tags.name: Labels
tags.description: Label groups that sort your email threads, for example Intent or Pricing questions. Heliyos files each classified thread under a group, and each group holds the more specific labels it brings together. The API calls them classification labels.

tags.name: Team
tags.description: The people in your workspace and their roles: joined members and pending invitations. Inviting someone sends them an email.

tags.name: Notification settings
tags.description: Which workspace events send notification emails, how often, and to whom. There is one settings document per workspace, shared by everyone in it.

message.description: A human-readable summary of the result.

get.description:
Returns the workspace your API key belongs to: its id and name, billing status, active plan,
member count, how many companies, people and deals it holds, and how many companies are watched
out of the plan's limit.

Counts are computed on every call, so they are always current.

parameters.description: Only entries recorded at or before this time, as an ISO 8601 date or date-time. A date alone means midnight UTC at the start of that day, so to include a whole day send the next day's midnight or `T23:59:59.999Z`.

get.description:
Returns the workspace's credit charges, newest first. Each entry says when credits were spent,
by which feature, how many, and on what. Use it to reconcile your balance or to see what a
worker run cost.

This list pages by page number: send `page` and `limit`. `meta.pagination` carries `page`,
`limit`, `offset` (rows skipped), `count` (all matching entries) and `hasMore`. There is no
cursor. To total a period, page through every entry for it and add up `creditsUtilized`.

Filters combine with AND. The API is read-only for usage: there is no way to add, change or
refund credits through it.

rules.description:
Up to 20 rules, each `{ "type", "value", "message" }`. Rule types:
- `minLength`, `maxLength`: string length, `value` a number.
- `pattern`: a regular expression the value must match, `value` a string of at most 200
  characters. A pattern that is invalid or could take exponential time (nested repetition
  such as `(a+)+`) is refused with 400.
- `email`: the value must be an email address (`value` is ignored).
- `min`, `max`: number bounds, `value` a number.

Other rule types are stored but not checked. Use string rules on text-like types and `min`
and `max` on number types.

post.description:
Adds a field to an object (base schema). Every existing record gets an empty value for the new
field. The response is the new field, not the whole object.


`type.type` decides what records can store. Send the `type` object shown, as the web app does.
Every type also accepts `""` or `null` as no value.

| `type.type` | Records store | Send as `type` | Extra configuration |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | A string, trimmed. | `{"type":"text","enum":["text","richText"]}` | None |
| `richText` | A string of formatted text. | `{"type":"richText","enum":["richText","text"]}` | None |
| `number` | A number. | `{"type":"number","enum":["number"]}` | `settings.abbreviateNumber` |
| `currency` | A number, the amount. | `{"type":"currency","enum":["number"]}` | `settings.currencyOptions`, `settings.abbreviateNumber` |
| `rating` | A number. The web app shows 1 to 5 stars; the API does not limit it. | `{"type":"rating","enum":["number"]}` | None |
| `checkbox` | `true` or `false`. | `{"type":"checkbox","enum":["boolean"]}` | None |
| `date` | A date, sent as an ISO 8601 string. | `{"type":"date","enum":["date","timestamp"]}` | None |
| `timestamp` | A date and time, sent as an ISO 8601 string. | `{"type":"timestamp","enum":["timestamp","date"]}` | None |
| `select` | One string. | `{"type":"select","enum":["select"]}` | `settings.selectOptions` |
| `multiSelect` | An array of strings. | `{"type":"multiSelect","enum":["multiSelect"]}` | `settings.selectOptions` |
| `url` | A URL. Must parse as a URI. | `{"type":"url","enum":["text"]}` | None |
| `email` | An email address. Must be valid. | `{"type":"email","enum":["text"]}` | None |
| `phone` | A string. The format is not checked. | `{"type":"phone","enum":["text"]}` | None |
| `user` | An array of workspace members. The web app stores `{ "id", "name", "email" }` per member, `id` being the user id. | `{"type":"user","enum":["user"]}` | None |
| `image` | An object. | `{"type":"image","enum":["text"]}` | None |
| `relationship` | Links to records of another object. | `{"type":"relationship","enum":["relationship"], ...}` | `type.relationshipSchemaId`, `type.relationshipConfig` |

Record writes check a `select` value is a string and a `multiSelect` value is an array; they do
not check them against `settings.selectOptions`. Relationship fields are best created in the web
app, which sets up both sides of the link; this endpoint stores the configuration on this object
only. `file` fields cannot be created through the API.


With `isAIEnabled: true` and an `aiPrompt`, workers fill the field. Send `runImmediately: true`
to start filling every record of the object straight away. That run uses credits for each
record it processes.


See Update a field for what can change after creation
and what each change does to stored values.

patch.description:
Changes one field of an object (base schema). Send at least one property; properties you leave
out are kept. Each property you send replaces the stored one completely: `settings`, `type`,
`permissions`, `validation`, `aiPrompt` and `default` are not merged, so send the whole object.
The response is the whole object with all of its fields.


| Change | Effect on records |
|---|---|
| `displayName`, `description`, `icon`, `isHiddenField`, `unique` | Display only. |
| `required`, `validation` | Apply to later record writes. Stored values are not re-checked. |
| `settings.selectOptions` | Replaces the options. Records holding a removed option keep it. On a board's lane field, lanes are added and removed to match. |
| `settings` (any key) | Replaces all settings: include the keys you want to keep. |
| `sequence` | Moves the field to that position (starting at 1); the fields in between shift by one. |
| `isAIEnabled` | Turns the AI column on or off and resets each record's AI status. Stored values are kept. |
| `type` | Refused with 400 while any record of the object holds a value for the field, including the empty value every record gets when a field is added. When accepted, stored values are not converted. |
| `name` (the key) | Values are not moved. See the warning. |
| `permissions` | Replaces who may view and edit the field. |

parameters.description:
A JSON object, URL-encoded, at most 20,000 characters. No key may start with `$` or contain a dot.
Keys:
- `search` (string): matches records where any field value contains the text, ignoring case.
  Text, numbers and booleans are searched; lists, objects and values longer than 100 characters
  are not. Results are not ranked by relevance; they keep the mode's order or your `sort`.
- `filters` (array, at most 500): conditions `{ "field", "operator", "value", "conjunction" }`.
  - `field`: a field key, or `createdAt`, `updatedAt` or `isAgentAssigned` (watched). Anything from
    the first `-` on is ignored. `<objectType>.<fieldKey>` (for example `company.company_name`)
    compares values stored on the record's links, not the linked record itself.
  - `operator`: `equals`, `notEquals` (exact match; text ignores case); `contains`, `notContains`,
    `startsWith`, `endsWith` (text, ignoring case; `value` must be a string, and a comma in a
    `contains` or `notContains` value means any or none of the parts); `empty`, `notEmpty`
    (missing, null or `""`; no value); `greaterThan`, `greaterThanOrEqual`, `lessThan`,
    `lessThanOrEqual` (numbers); `after`, `before` (dates, the same as `greaterThan` and
    `lessThan`). Any other operator is treated as an exact match on the raw value.
  - `value`: a string, number or boolean. A string that looks like a number is compared as a number.
    Date fields are stored as text, so send ISO 8601 dates (`2026-12-31`). For `createdAt` and
    `updatedAt` the value is read as a date, and `equals` matches the whole day.
  - `conjunction`: `and` (default) or `or`. The first condition's is ignored; every other condition
    must use the same one. Mixing `and` and `or` is a 400.
- `sort` (array): `{ "field", "direction" }`, with the same field names as conditions and
  direction `asc` or `desc`. Text sorts ignore case. Sorting by `<objectType>.<fieldKey>` leaves
  out records without a link of that type.
- `page` (integer, at least 1) and `pageSize` (integer, at least 1): page-number paging.
- `bypassPageSizeCap` (boolean): raises the page size cap from 100 to 5000.
- `isAgentAssigned` (boolean): `true` for watched records only, `false` for the others.
- `enrich` (boolean, default `true`): `false` leaves out linked records' values and returns 0 for
  the activity counts. Faster for pickers.
- `viewType` (`kanban`) with `kanbanConfig.groupByField` (a field key, default `status`): return
  a board grouped by that field.

200.description: A page of records, or a board when `filters.viewType` is `kanban`.

message.description: A human-readable summary of the result.

data.description: The records. With `"viewType": "kanban"`, an array of `RecordKanbanColumn` instead.

400.description: VALIDATION_FAILED: `filters` is not a JSON object, carries a `$` or dotted key, mixes `and` and `or`, gives a text operator a non-string value, or `cursor` is sent with a sort or a board. A query the database rejects (for example a malformed sort) answers "Error fetching records".

get.description:
Returns the records of one object (base schema), such as your companies, people, deals or a custom
object. Get the object's id and its field keys from the Objects endpoints.

Each record's `data` holds only the object's fields. A field you may not view comes back as `null`.
Every record also carries its links in `relationships` (each with the linked record's field values in
`data`) and counts of linked comments, notes and open tasks.

**Paging.** There are two modes.

- **Cursor (default).** Send `limit` (1 to 100, default 20). Records come newest first (by creation).
  When `meta.pagination.next_cursor` is present, send it back as `cursor` for the next page.
- **Page number.** Used as soon as you send `page` (query or `filters`), `filters.pageSize`, a
  `filters.sort` or a board (`"viewType": "kanban"`). Without a sort, records come most recently
  updated first. `meta.pagination` is `{ page, limit, totalPages, count, hasMore }`, where `count` is
  the number of matching records and `limit` is the page size actually used. A `cursor` together
  with a sort or a board is a 400.

**Page size in page-number mode** is `filters.pageSize`, or `limit` when you do not send one. It is
capped at 100. With `"bypassPageSizeCap": true` it can go up to 5000, for callers that need a
complete set in one response. A `pageSize` above 200 (5000 with the bypass) is clamped rather than
rejected.

**Filtering.** Send a JSON object in `filters`, URL-encoded. Its keys are described on the parameter
below. For example, deals in negotiation worth at least 50,000 that mention "northwind", soonest
close date first, 50 per page:

```json
{
  "search": "northwind",
  "filters": [
    {
      "field": "stage",
      "operator": "equals",
      "value": "Negotiation"
    },
    {
      "field": "deal_value",
      "operator": "greaterThanOrEqual",
      "value": 50000,
      "conjunction": "and"
    }
  ],
  "sort": [
    {
      "field": "close_date",
      "direction": "asc"
    }
  ],
  "page": 1,
  "pageSize": 50
}
```

`curl -G --data-urlencode` encodes the JSON into the query string for you:

```bash
curl -G "https://api-prod.heliyos.ai/v1/platform/base-schemas/66a0f1e2d3c4b5a697880003/records" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer heliyos_..." \
  --data-urlencode 'filters={
    "search": "northwind",
    "filters": [
      {
        "field": "stage",
        "operator": "equals",
        "value": "Negotiation"
      },
      {
        "field": "deal_value",
        "operator": "greaterThanOrEqual",
        "value": 50000,
        "conjunction": "and"
      }
    ],
    "sort": [
      {
        "field": "close_date",
        "direction": "asc"
      }
    ],
    "page": 1,
    "pageSize": 50
  '}'
```

**Boards.** With `"viewType": "kanban"` the response groups records by a field instead of paging
them: `data` is an array of `RecordKanbanColumn` (`columnId`, `items`, `pagination`) holding every
matching record, and `meta.pagination` is `{ page, limit, totalCount }`.

See [Pagination](/api-reference/pagination) and [Filtering and sorting](/api-reference/filtering).

Creates a record in an object. Send the field values at the top level of the body, keyed by the
object's field keys (for example `company_name`, `website`, `people_name`, `email`, `deal_name`,
`stage`), and the ids of records to link in `relationships`.

**Values by field type.** Every type also accepts `null` and `""`.

| Field type | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `text`, `richText`, `phone`, `select` | A string. A `select` value is not checked against the field's options. |
| `email` | An email address. |
| `url` | A full URI, for example `https://northwind.example`. |
| `number`, `currency`, `rating` | A number. |
| `checkbox` | `true` or `false`. |
| `date`, `timestamp` | An ISO 8601 date or date-time string. It is stored as sent. |
| `multiSelect` | An array of strings. |
| `user` | An array. The app stores team members as `{ "id", "firstName", "lastName", "email" }`. |
| `image` | An object. |
| `file` | An array of `{ "fileName", "url" }` objects, optionally with `attachmentId`, `fileSize`, `mimeType`, `storageKey`, `uploadedAt`. |
| `relationship` | Any value. |

- Fields the object marks required must be included.
- Only fields you may edit are written. Other keys, including keys that are not fields of the object,
  are dropped without an error. Keys that start with `$` or contain a dot are dropped too.
- Field keys with a dot, such as `company.company_name` on people and deals, show a linked record's
  value. Set them by linking that record in `relationships`.

- Companies start with `account_status` and `engagement_status` set to `unknown` unless you send them,
  and get a `logo` built from `website` when you send no logo. Companies and people start with
  `enrichmentStatus` `NOT_ENRICHED`.

  same object is refused with a 409.

type) event, which can start workers that subscribe to it. A new deal sends the workspace's deal
notification email when deal notifications are on. Companies, people and deals are sent to HubSpot
when the workspace syncs with it. A new company is enriched automatically when automatic enrichment
is on (Settings, Autopilot), which uses credits.

post.description:
Starts Heliyos workers on a task now, the same as pressing Play on the task. The call takes no body.

What it does, in order:
1. Clears the task's paused flag and, unless the task is `completed` or `cancelled`, moves it to
   `in_progress` (and sets `isFinished` to false).
2. Looks for a run already open on the task (`queued`, `running`, `paused`, `awaiting_approval` or
   `waiting`). If there is one, it is returned with `triggered: false` and no new run starts. A
   `queued` or `running` run that has written nothing for 20 minutes is treated as dead and does not count.
3. Otherwise starts a new run with `triggered: true` and status `queued`. The run starts even when no
   worker subscribes to new tasks, and it cancels any wake-up a worker had scheduled for the task.

The call returns as soon as the run is queued. Follow it with `GET /v1/platform/workers/runs/{id}`
using `orchestratorRunId`.

**Credits.** Each time the run calls one of your custom workers, the workspace is charged a fixed
number of credits; Heliyos's built-in workers are free. If the workspace cannot cover a custom worker
call when the run starts, nothing starts and the call answers 409. Actions the workers take (for
example enrichment) can use credits of their own.

**Reviews.** Workers write companies, people, tasks, notes and email drafts directly. Deal changes,
sending email, booking meetings, actions in connected apps and anything a worker asks you to decide
wait for a person's review unless the workspace's autopilot settings allow them, and even then a call
below the confidence threshold still waits. While an action waits, the run's status is `awaiting_approval`.

**Idempotency.** Calling again while a run is open returns that run. The check is not atomic, so two
calls at the same moment can start two runs.

post.description:
Sends a message to Heliyos, the same as typing it into Ask Heliyos in the app. Heliyos reads the
workspace, plans, and calls workers to do the work. It can answer a question ("summarise what
changed with Contoso this week") or carry out a job ("draft a follow-up to the Fabrikam thread").

**What it returns.** The call starts a run and answers with `runId`, `status` and `threadId`.
With `wait` above 0 it holds the request for up to that many seconds until the run settles:
finishes, or stops to wait on a person or a schedule. If the run completes in time, `output`
carries the reply. Otherwise follow the run:

1. Call **Get a run** with the `runId` and `wait=30`. Repeat while
   `status` is `queued` or `running`.
2. When `status` is `completed`, read `output.response`. On `failed`, read `error` with
   `include=detail`.
3. When `status` is `awaiting_approval`, `paused`, `waiting` or `scheduled`, polling will not
   move it. A person has to act in Heliyos (Review), or the scheduled time has to come.

**List runs** with `threadId` returns every run of a conversation.

**Conversations.** Leave `threadId` out to start a new conversation; Heliyos returns its id.
Send it back to continue. If the thread's run is still open, your message joins that run instead
of starting another: it is queued while the run works, read after the decision while it waits
for a review, and resumes it when it is paused.

**Reviews.** Consequential actions, such as sending an email or changing a deal, wait for a
person's approval unless the workspace's autopilot allows them. The run then shows
`awaiting_approval` and lists the reviews in `reviews`.

**Credits.** Each call to a custom worker during the run spends credits once the call finishes.
Default workers and Heliyos's own reasoning are free. Tools the run uses can spend credits too,
for example company enrichment. The run's total is in `usage.credits` on **Get a run**, and each
charge is in **List credit usage** under `worker_run`.

**Timeouts.** `wait` is at most 90 seconds; set your HTTP client's timeout above it (120 seconds
is safe). A run has no fixed time limit and keeps working after the call returns. If you
disconnect early, the run is not affected.

Every call starts or continues work: calling twice with the same message runs it twice.

worker**. The whole catalogue comes back in one response; it is not paged.

Every workspace has the same shared triggers. A workspace can also have entries of its own,
listed after the shared ones; an own entry with the same `name` as a shared one replaces it.

**From catalogue entry to worker trigger.**

| Catalogue entry | Trigger object on the worker |
| --- | --- |
| `kind` `event`, for example `deal.updated` | `{ "type": "event", "events": ["deal.updated"] }`. One trigger can list several event names; `"*"` means every event. |
| `kind` `mention` (`mention`) | `{ "type": "mention" }`. Every active worker answers mentions, with or without it. |
| `kind` `schedule` (`schedule`) | `{ "type": "scheduled", "match": { "schedule": "0 8 * * 1-5", "timezone": "Europe/Berlin" } }` for a repeating 5-field cron, or `match.at` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` local time) with `match.timezone` for one run. |
| Not in the catalogue | `{ "type": "task_created" }` runs on every new task; `match.taskType` limits it to some task types. |

**Things to know.**
- The API does not check event names against this catalogue when you save a worker. A name
  that is not in it never fires.
- Triggers with an `integration` only fire while that app is connected (`integration.connected`).
- `company.attribute_updated`, `people.attribute_updated` and `deal.attribute_updated` watch
  fields picked in the Heliyos app. Created through the API, they run on a change to any field
  of that object.
- A trigger with `type` `scheduled` is registered when you save the worker; check
  `scheduleSync` in that response.

post.description:
Records a person's decision on a pending review and acts on it. A review is decided once.

**Approving** carries out the worker's action:
- `deal_update` and `classification_label`: Heliyos applies the change before it answers, the same way an
  edit in Heliyos would, and reports it in `applied`. If applying fails, nothing is recorded and the review
  stays pending.
- A saved email draft (`origin: artifact`): the draft is sent before the call answers. If sending fails, the
  approval is still recorded and `orchestrator.error` says why.
- Every other type: the worker's run resumes in the background and carries out the action. This happens only
  once every pending review of that run is decided (`orchestrator.pending` counts the rest). Read the run, or
  the review's `outcome`, to see the result. If the run is no longer waiting, the decision is recorded and
  nothing runs.

**Rejecting** drops the action and tells the worker your `feedback`. A saved email draft is discarded. As
with approval, a paused run resumes, without the action, once every review it waits on is decided.

**Changing the proposal before approving.** For `deal_update`, send the fields to write in `data` (and
`relationships` or `schemaId`). For other paused actions, send the changed arguments in `args`. They are
checked by the same rules as the worker's; if they fail, the action does not run and `outcome.error`
says why. `data`, `relationships`, `schemaId` and `args` are ignored on rejection. A saved email draft is
sent as saved: `args` does not change it.

**Already decided.** A review that is not pending answers 400 and nothing happens, so sending a decision
again after it succeeded does not repeat the action. Send one decision at a time per review: of two
decisions sent at the same moment on a deal or label review, one wins and the other answers 409.

**Who can decide.** Any member of the workspace, and any API key. A decision made with an API key counts as
a person's: it is recorded under the user who created the key and carried out exactly as if that person
had approved it in Heliyos. Deciding is blocked while the workspace's subscription is inactive.

`meta.message` is `Review approved.` or `Review rejected.`. When a deal or label change was applied but the
run could not be told yet, it is `Review approved; the change is applied, but the agent run could not be
notified.` and `orchestratorError` is set: the run picks the decision up later on its own.

Office and OpenDocument files (`application/msword`,
`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document`,
`application/vnd.ms-excel`, `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`,
`application/vnd.ms-powerpoint`,
`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation`,
`application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text`, `application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.spreadsheet`,
`application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.presentation`), `application/rtf`, text and data
(`text/plain`, `text/csv`, `text/tab-separated-values`, `text/markdown`, `application/json`,
`text/calendar`, `message/rfc822`), audio (`audio/mpeg`, `audio/mp4`, `audio/x-m4a`,

Returns the workspace's notification settings: whether notifications are on, who receives them,
and which events notify and how often.

These are workspace settings, not settings of the person who owns the API key. Everyone in the
workspace reads and edits the same document.

A workspace that has never saved settings has none: the response then has `data: {}` and
`meta.message` "No notification settings found.", and no notification emails are sent (except
`integration.not_synced`).

patch.description:
Changes the workspace's notification settings, creating them the first time. Send at least one
field. Each field you send replaces that setting completely; fields you leave out are kept.

- `eventTypes` is the full list of notifying events. To add one event, read the current list,
  add to it and send the whole list back.
- `notifyEmails` is the full recipient list. Changing who receives notifications needs an owner
  or admin (an API key counts as an admin). Sending the stored list back unchanged is allowed for
  anyone who can edit the settings. A list can grow to at most 10 addresses.
- The first save of a workspace that had no settings starts from notifications on, no
  recipients and no events, then applies what you sent.

What spent the credits. Values written today:
- `worker_run`: a custom worker called during a run (default workers are free).
- `company_enrichment`: a company was enriched.
- `people_enrichment`: people were enriched for a lead set.
- `leadset_enrichment`: lead set columns were enriched.

organizationId.description: The workspace the task belongs to.

title.description: The task's title. Can be an empty string.

description.description: The task's body, as plain text or markdown.

isFinished.description: A done flag kept beside `status`. Heliyos does not derive it from `status`: set it yourself when you complete or reopen a task.

dueDate.description: When the task is due. Absent when none is set.

assignedUser.description: The people assigned to the task.

assignedAgents.description: The workers assigned to the task.

relationships.description: The records the task is linked to. In list and get responses each entry is hydrated with the record's field values in `data` and its object in `schema`.

currentRunId.description: The id of the workers' current or last run on the task.

artifactsCount.description: Files linked to the task. List and get only.

agentPaused.description: True when workers are paused on this task. Starting a run clears it.

agentRun.description: The last note a worker left on the task (`note`, `runId`, `agent`, `at`).

planCheckpoints.description: The steps of the workers' plan for the task, each with `id`, `title`, `description`, `worker`, `note` and `status` (`pending`, `running`, `completed`, `failed` or `skipped`).

hubspotTaskId.description: The linked HubSpot task id, when the workspace syncs tasks with HubSpot.

TaskRelationshipInput.description: A record to link the task to.

objectId.description: Id of the linked record, task, note or interaction. Must belong to this workspace.

schemaId.description: The linked record's object (base schema) id. Recommended for records. Empty or null is dropped.

objectType.description: `company`, `people`, `deals` or a custom object type for records; `task`, `note` or `interaction` otherwise.

data.description: An optional display snapshot of the record, stored as sent. Get and list replace it with the record's current values.

triggered.description: True when this call started a new run. False when a run already open on the task was returned instead.

orchestratorRunId.description: The run's id. Follow it with `GET /v1/platform/workers/runs/{id}`.

status.description: The run's status: `queued` for a new run; for an existing run, its current status (`queued`, `running`, `paused`, `awaiting_approval` or `waiting`).

WorkerTriggerInput.description: One thing that starts the worker.

type.description:
- `task_created`: the worker runs when a task is created. `match.taskType` limits it to some task types.
- `mention`: the worker runs when someone mentions it in chat. Every active worker answers mentions, with or without this entry; `match.mentionPattern` is kept with it.
- `event`: the worker runs on the named events in `events`, for example `task.created`,
  `deal.updated`, `email.received`, `meeting.completed` or `company.attribute_updated`.
  `*` means every event. An event name that Heliyos never emits never matches.
- `scheduled`: the worker runs on a schedule. Put a 5-field cron in `match.schedule` (UTC unless
  `match.timezone` is set), or a one-time local time in `match.at` with `match.timezone`.
- `webhook`: older spelling of `event`, with the event name in `match.webhookEvent`. Saved as `event`.
- `schedule`: older spelling of `scheduled`. Saved as `scheduled`.
- `playground`: used by test runs in the Heliyos app. Has no effect when set through the API.

source.description: Accepted and ignored. Triggers you send are always saved with `source` `user`.

events.description: `event` triggers only: the event names to run on. Up to 200 names of up to 200 characters.

match.description:
Conditions and timing. These keys are stored; any other key is dropped:
- `taskType` (array of strings): `task_created` only, the task types to run on.
- `taskStatus` (string): a task status condition.
- `mentionPattern` (string): `mention` only, text the mention must contain.
- `webhookEvent` (string or array): `webhook` only, the event names.
- `schedule` (string): `scheduled` only, a 5-field cron such as `0 8 * * 1-5`.
- `at` (string): `scheduled` only, a one-time local wall time `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`.
- `timezone` (string): an IANA zone such as `Europe/Berlin` for `schedule` or `at`. Default UTC.
- `recurrence` (object): the Heliyos app's own description of the schedule, so its editor can reopen it.

dependencies.description: Ids of other workers in this workspace that must finish before this one starts. Up to 50.

WorkerTrigger.description: A stored trigger. Event subscriptions are stored as `event`, schedules as `scheduled`.

type.description: `task_created`, `mention`, `event`, `scheduled` or `playground`. Workers saved long ago can still show `webhook` or `schedule`.

source.description: `default`: built into a default worker. It stays when you change the worker's triggers. `user`: added by a person or the API, removable.

match.description: Conditions and timing, as in the trigger input.

WorkerResources.description: The knowledge files the worker reads.

scope.description:
The file scope picked in the Heliyos app: `everything` (the default), `org_knowledge`
(knowledge base files), `account_files` (files on records) or `selected_files` (files you
pick). Which knowledge base files the worker reads is set by `allKbFiles` and
`linkedKbFileIds`.

allKbFiles.description: `true` links every knowledge base file of the workspace. When absent, every file is linked unless `linkedKbFileIds` names some.

linkedKbFileIds.description: Knowledge base files linked to the worker. Each must be a file of this workspace. Up to 1,000.

fileIds.description: Other files picked for the worker. Each must be a file of this workspace. Up to 1,000.

organizationId.description: The workspace the worker belongs to.

name.description: The worker's name, unique in the workspace.

type.description: `default`: built into every workspace. Only its instructions, description, icon, active flag, memory and its own triggers can change, and it cannot be deleted. `custom`: created by you, fully editable and deletable.

isActive.description: `false` pauses the worker: nothing starts it and Heliyos does not call it.

icon.description: The icon the Heliyos app shows for the worker.

isExcluded.description: `true` for older built-in workers that run on a separate pipeline. They are listed for reference, and Heliyos never calls them.

description.description: One line that tells Heliyos (and people) what the worker is for. Heliyos reads it to decide when to call the worker.

instructions.description: What the worker does and how, in Markdown.

toolName.description: The stable snake_case name Heliyos calls the worker by. Set on create and never changed.

toolNames.description: The built-in tools the worker may use, by name.

actionIds.description: The workspace actions the worker may run.

toolPolicy.description: Limits on what the worker may do.

readOnly.description: `true`: the worker may read but never change data.

enabled.description: `true`: the worker keeps memory across runs.

triggers.description: What starts the worker. An empty list means it only runs when Heliyos or a person calls it.

schedule.description: Legacy cron list. Schedules live on `scheduled` triggers now.

runtime.description: How Heliyos runs the worker. Set by Heliyos, read-only.

WorkerScheduleSync.description: What happened to the worker's schedules after the save. The worker is saved even when a schedule fails, but a failed schedule never fires: check `failed`.

created.description: Ids of the worker's schedules that are registered after this save, including ones that already existed. A one-time `at` in the past is skipped and not listed.

deleted.description: Ids of schedules removed by this save because no trigger asks for them any more.

failed.description: One line per schedule that could not be registered. Empty when every schedule is in place.

final_response_by.description: Who wrote the reply, Heliyos or the worker that owned the answer.

runId.description: The run that handles your message. Follow it with **Get a run**. `null` only when no run could be found for the message (status `not_found`).

status.description:
With `wait` 0, what happened to the message:
- `queued`: a new run started, or the message was queued on the thread's running run.
- `queued_until_decision`: the thread's run waits for a review; your message is read after the decision.
- `resuming`: the thread's paused or waiting run resumed with your message.
- `already_running`: the thread's run was already working, and your message may not have
  reached it. Follow the run, then send the message again once it settles.
- `not_found`: the thread's run disappeared before the message reached it. Nothing ran; send again.

With `wait` above 0, the run's own status when the call returns (see **Get a run** for every
value). A run that is still working returns `running` or `queued`.

threadId.description: The conversation. Send it back as `threadId` to continue it. Heliyos makes one up when you send none.

output.description: The run's final reply, present when the run produced one within `wait`.

seq.description: The step's position in the run, starting at 1.

type.description:
What the step was: `worker` (a worker was called), `tool` (a tool call), `approval` (a review
was raised), `wait` and `wakeup` (the run scheduled a wait and woke up), `handoff`, `final`
(the reply). Older or light runs can show other kinds.

title.description: The worker, tool or step label.

status.description: The step's status, for example `pending`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `waiting`, `approved` or `rejected`.

endedAt.description: When the step ended. `null` while it runs.

summary.description: The first 200 characters of the step's error, else of its result's text. `null` when the result is raw data.

WorkerRunReview.description: A review the run raised. Reviews are decided by a person in Heliyos, under Review.

status.description:
- `PENDING`: waiting for a person.
- `PROCESSING`: decided, and the decision is being carried out.
- `APPROVED`: approved. The run goes on with the action.
- `REJECTED`: rejected. The run goes on without it.

type.description: What is being reviewed, for example `email_draft` (an email to send), `deal_update` (a deal change), `meeting_scheduled` or `classification_label`. The set is open: an action from a connected app uses its own name. See [List reviews](/api-reference/reviews/list-reviews).

WorkerRunUsage.description: What the run used. Counters appear once there is something to count.

credits.description: Credits charged to the workspace by this run (custom worker calls).

WorkerRunTrigger.description: What set the run off, without its payload.

type.description: The trigger kind, for example `chat`, `event`, `mention`, `task_created` or `scheduled`.

objectType.description: The kind of record the trigger named, for example `task`, `company` or `interaction`.

status.description:
Still going:
- `queued`: created, about to start.
- `running`: working now.

Waiting on a person or a schedule (it will not move until that happens):
- `awaiting_approval`: paused on one or more reviews in `reviews`. It resumes when every one is decided.
- `paused`: paused by a person. It resumes when someone resumes it or sends a message on its thread.
- `waiting`: it set itself a wait and wakes up at the scheduled time.
- `scheduled`: it waits for a scheduled time.

Finished, never changes again:
- `completed`: done. `output` has the reply.
- `failed`: stopped on an error. Read `error` (with `include=detail`) and the failed step.
- `skipped`: did not run, for example because the same event already started a run.
- `cancelled`: cancelled before it finished.
- `stopped`: stopped by a person.

endedAt.description: When it finished. `null` until it is in a finished status.

threadId.description: The conversation the run belongs to, for chat runs.

taskId.description: The task the run works on, for task runs.

steps.description: Every step so far, in order.

reviews.description: The reviews the run raised, oldest first.

usage.description: Credits and model usage so far.

output.description: The run's final reply, once it has one.

agentName.description: `include=detail` only: who planned the run, Heliyos or the worker it focused on.

surface.description: `include=detail` only: where the run started. See `surface` on **List runs**.

workers.description: `include=detail` only: the workers that took part.

nodeId.description: The worker's step in the run.

status.description: The worker's status in this run.

toolCalls.description: `include=detail` only: how many tool calls the run made.

createdAt.description: `include=detail` only: when the run was created.

graph.description: `include=step_payloads` only: the run's full execution graph (`nodes`, `edges`).

WorkerRunListItem.description: A run as stored, without its step log and execution graph. Read one run with **Get a run** for its steps. Runs can carry more fields than these; treat unknown ones as internal and subject to change.

orchestratorRunId.description: The run id. Pass it to **Get a run**.

status.description: The run's status. See `status` on **Get a run** for every value.

title.description: A short title for the run.

surface.description: Where the run started: `chat` (Ask Heliyos), `worker_chat`, `task_chat`, `background` (an event, schedule or task) or `worker_direct`.

agentName.description: The worker the run focused on, when there was one.

userInput.description: The message that started a chat run, up to 4,000 characters.

trigger.description: The trigger that started the run, with its payload.

triggerRef.description: The trigger kind and the record it named.

objectType.description: The record's kind, for example `company`, `people`, `deals`, `task` or `interaction`.

taskId.description: The task the run works on.

userId.description: The person who started the run, for chat runs.

toolCalls.description: How many tool calls the run made.

finalOutput.description: The final reply, once there is one.

WorkerIntegrationLink.description: The connected app that delivers this trigger or performs this action. Present only when one does; Heliyos's own triggers and tools have none.

title.description: The app's name, for example `Gmail`, `Outlook`, `Google Drive`, `OneDrive`, `HubSpot` or `Typeform`. Where two apps can do the job (email and calendar through Gmail or Outlook), the connected one is named; with neither connected, the first one is.

iconSrc.description: The app's logo URL. Absent when Heliyos has no logo for it.

connected.description: `true` when the workspace has this app connected and working now. While it is `false`, the trigger does not fire and the action cannot work. Connect the app in Heliyos first.

WorkerTriggerCatalogEntry.description: One trigger a worker can be set to run on.

organizationId.description: `null` for the triggers every workspace has. A workspace's own entry carries its id.

name.description: The trigger's name. For a `kind` `event` entry, this is the event name you put in a trigger's `events`, for example `deal.updated`.

kind.description:
How the entry maps to a trigger on **Create a worker** and **Update a worker**:
- `event`: add `name` to the `events` of a trigger with `type` `event`.
- `mention`: a trigger with `type` `mention`. Every active worker answers mentions anyway.
- `schedule`: a trigger with `type` `scheduled` and a cron or one-time `at` in `match`.

label.description: A short name for the trigger, as the Heliyos app shows it.

description.description: When the trigger fires, in a sentence.

objectType.description: What the event is about: `interaction` (an email or meeting), `task`, `company`, `people`, `deals`, `note`, `baseschema` (an object's fields), `review`, `scout` or `signal`. `null` for `mention` and `schedule`.

source.description: Where the event comes from. `platform`: a change made in Heliyos, by a person, the API or a worker. `internal`: Heliyos's own background work, such as inbox sync or research. Any other value names the service that delivers the event. Informational: read `integration` to know whether a connected app is needed.

provider.description: A key for the app that delivers the event. Present on entries that have `integration`.

providerRef.description: The app's own name for the event, on entries that come from a connected app.

selectsAttributes.description: `true` on `company.attribute_updated`, `people.attribute_updated` and `deal.attribute_updated`: in the Heliyos app you pick the fields to watch. The API stores only the `match` keys listed on **Create a worker**, so such a subscription created through the API runs when any field of that object changes.

isActive.description: Absent or `true`. Inactive entries are not listed.

WorkerAction.description: One action a worker can take. The API calls actions tools: `toolNames` and `actionIds` on a worker hold them.

name.description: The action's stable snake_case name, for example `create_task` or `send_email`. For a `builtin` action, this is the value you put in a worker's `toolNames`.

label.description: A short, readable name, as a run's activity shows it (for example `Created task`).

display_name.description: `action` only: the action's name as the connected app's set of actions defines it, for example `Send Email`. `null` for `builtin`.

description.description: What the action does, as the worker reads it when deciding whether to use it. Can be long.

source.description:
- `builtin`: one of Heliyos's own actions (reading and writing records, tasks and notes, web
  research, files, charts, follow-ups). Put `name` in the worker's `toolNames`.
- `action`: an action of your workspace, performed by a connected app (email, calendar, file
  storage and so on). Put `action_id` in the worker's `actionIds`.

action_id.description: `action` only: the action's id, the value for `actionIds`. `null` for `builtin`.

provider.description: `action` only: a key for the app that performs it. Read `integration` for the app's name and status. `null` for `builtin`.

risk.description:
What kind of action it is, which decides whether a call waits for a person's review:
- `read`: reads only. Never waits.
- `write_crm`: writes companies, people, tasks, notes, documents, email drafts and thread or
  meeting analysis. Applies directly, never waits. A saved email draft then waits for review
  before it is sent.
- `write_deal`: creates or changes a deal. Waits unless autopilot approves deal changes.
- `communicate`: sends email. Waits unless autopilot sends email.
- `schedule_meeting`: books, moves or cancels a meeting. Waits unless autopilot schedules meetings.
- `external`: changes something in a connected app. Waits unless autopilot allows external
  actions (off by default).
- `schedule`: schedules or cancels a follow-up run. Runs unless autopilot follow-ups are turned off (on by default).
- `plan`: submits a plan. Waits only when the workspace requires plan approval.
- `confirm`: asks a person a question or for approval. Always waits.

Even with autopilot on for a kind of action, a call waits when the worker's stated confidence
is below the threshold set for it (80 by default) or when it states none.

review_type.description: The kind of review a call raises when it waits, for example `email_draft`, `deal_update` or `meeting_scheduled`. Defaults to the action's `name`.

common.description: `true`: every worker has this action, whatever its `toolNames` say. You do not need to list it.

is_hidden.description: `true`: Heliyos wires this action in where it is needed. It is not offered for picking in the Heliyos app; leave it out of a worker's configuration.

input.description: The JSON Schema of the action's input, as the worker fills it in.

output.description: The JSON Schema of the action's result.

ReviewObjectRef.description: A record or task the review is about.

objectId.description: Id of the record or task.

name.description: The record's display name, when the worker could resolve it.

ReviewApproval.description: The decision. This is the review's authoritative status.

status.description:
- `PENDING`: waiting for a person.
- `PROCESSING`: a decision on a `deal_update` or `classification_label` review is being applied right now. It moves to `APPROVED` or `REJECTED` within the same request, or back to `PENDING` if applying failed.
- `APPROVED`: approved by a person, or let through by the workspace's autopilot settings (then `by` is `autopilot`).
- `REJECTED`: rejected by a person.

by.description: Id of the user who decided. A decision made with an API key is recorded under the user who created the key. `autopilot` when the workspace's autopilot settings approved the action without a person. Null while pending.

at.description: When it was decided. Null while pending.

comment.description: The reviewer's note, kept on the review.

feedback.description: What the reviewer told the worker, for example why it was rejected.

editedArgs.description: The action's arguments as the reviewer changed them on approval, when they changed any.

Review.description: A worker action waiting for, or decided by, a person. Fields beyond the common ones depend on `type`. Reviews raised before a field existed may not carry it.

id.description: The review's id, the same value as `_id`.

organizationId.description: The workspace the review belongs to.

type.description:
What is being reviewed. The set is open: actions in connected apps and actions your workspace defines
use their own name. Common values:
- `email_draft`: an email to send.
- `deal_update`: a deal to create (`dealAction: Create`) or change (`dealAction: Update`).
- `meeting_scheduled`: a meeting to book or reschedule.
- `task`: a task to create or change.
- `document`: a file to save on a record or task.
- `note`: a note to create.
- `object_create`, `object_update`: a record other than a deal to create or change.
- `schedule`: a scheduled wake-up for a worker to create or cancel.
- `plan`: a plan the worker wants approved before it acts.
- `decision`: a question the worker asked (`kind: question`) or an approval it asked for before going on.
- `classification_label`: a new label to create.

kind.description:
- `action`: a paused action. Approving lets it run.
- `plan`: a plan. Approving lets the worker carry it out.
- `question`: a question for a person. Answer it in `feedback`.
- `approval`: a saved email draft. Approving sends it.

origin.description:
- `model`: the worker's run is paused on this action and resumes when it is decided.
- `artifact`: the work is already saved (an email draft on its thread) and the decision acts on it. The run does not wait for it.
- `autopilot`: the action ran without a person under the workspace's autopilot settings. Kept for the record, already `APPROVED`.

status.description: The decision, mirrored from `approval.status`. Read `approval.status` for the current value.

agent.description: The name of the worker that raised the review.

agentRef.description: The worker that raised the review.

id.description: The worker's id. Null when Heliyos itself raised it.

name.description: The worker's name.

runId.description: The run that raised the review. Read it with `GET /v1/platform/workers/runs/{id}`. A pending review a later run proposed again points at that later run.

agentRunId.description: The same value as `runId`, under its older name.

previousRunId.description: The run the review pointed at before a later run proposed the same change again.

revisions.description: How many times a later run replaced the proposal while the review was pending.

surface.description: Where the run that raised it started, for example `chat` or `background`.

taskId.description: The task the run worked on, when it worked on one.

threadId.description: The chat conversation the run belongs to, when it started in chat.

tool.description: The action the worker wants to take.

name.description: The action's name, for example `send_email` or `schedule_meeting`.

callId.description: Identifies this one call within the run.

title.description: A one-line title, for example `Send email: Renewal terms`.

summary.description: The proposal in a sentence or two.

args.description: The action's arguments as the worker proposed them. Send changed values in `args` when you approve.

confidence.description: How sure the worker said it was, from 0 to 100. Null when it did not say.

reasoning.description: Why the worker proposes the action, in its own words. Empty when it gave no reason.

approvalReason.description: Why the action waits for a person, for example because approval is required for this kind of action or the stated confidence is below the workspace's threshold.

objectRefs.description: The records and tasks the review is about.

dealAction.description: `deal_update`: whether the deal is new or an existing one changes. `meeting_scheduled`: `Create` for a new meeting, `Update` for a reschedule.

previousVersion.description: `deal_update` with `Update`: the deal as it is now (`_id`, `data`, `relationships`). Null for a new deal.

newVersion.description: `deal_update`: the deal as it would be if approved (`data`, `relationships`, and for a new deal the `schemaId` of its pipeline). After an approval with edited fields, the fields as approved.

draftEmail.description: `email_draft`: the email (`subject`, `body`, `from`, `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `attachments`, and `interactionThreadId`, the email thread it belongs to). Recipients are email addresses or `{ email, name }` objects.

draft.description: `email_draft` with `origin: artifact`: where the saved draft lives (`interactionId` of the email thread, `messageId`).

meetingDetails.description: `meeting_scheduled`: the proposed event (`title`, `startTime`, `endTime`, `timezone`, `participants`, `description`, `location`, `conferencing` and the rest of the event's fields).

taskMeta.description: `task`: the task (`title`, `objectId` of an existing task, `status`, `dueDate`, `description`).

documentMeta.description: `document`: the file (`fileName`, `description`, and when it can be opened, `url`, `mimeType`, `size`, `objectAttachmentId`).

categoryName.description: `classification_label`: the name of the label to create.

outcome.description: What happened after the decision. `ok` (whether it worked), `at`, and `error` when it failed. For an action a run carried out, `result` with what the action returned. For a deal or label Heliyos applied on approval, `appliedBy: platform` with `action`, `dealId` or `labelId`. Absent until something happened.

metadata.description: When the review was raised and last changed.

ReviewDetail.description: A review, with the records and work it refers to resolved.

relatedObjects.description: The company, people and deal records the review is about: those in `objectRefs` and those linked to the email thread or meeting it sits on. Full records, at most 50.

interactionData.description: The email thread or meeting `objectRef` points at, when it points at one.

taskData.description: The task `taskMeta.objectId` (or `objectRef`) points at, when it points at one.

previousVersionRelatedObjects.description: `deal_update`: the records linked to the deal as it is now.

newVersionRelatedObjects.description: `deal_update`: the records linked to the deal as proposed.

applied.description: Approved `deal_update` and `classification_label` reviews only: what Heliyos changed before answering. For a deal, `action` (`Create` or `Update`), `dealId`, `schemaId` and `object` (the deal as saved). For a label, `action` (`Create`, or `Exists` when a label with that name was already there), `labelId` and `name`.

orchestrator.description:
What the worker run did with the decision:
- `runId` and `resuming: true`: this was the last pending review of the run, which now resumes and carries out (or drops) the action.
- `runId` and `pending`: the run still waits on this many other reviews. Nothing runs until they are decided.
- `runId` alone: the run is no longer waiting, so nothing resumes.
- `sent`: for a saved email draft, whether it was sent.
- `error`: for a saved email draft, why sending or discarding failed. The decision is still recorded.

orchestratorError.description: Present when a deal or label change was applied and recorded but the worker run could not be told yet. The run picks the decision up later on its own.

ScoutAuditMetadata.description: When the Scout was created and last changed. `by` is a service label such as `system`, not a user id.

by.description: Who last changed it, for example `system`.

ScoutOutputSchema.description:
The structured output a custom Scout asks for on each run, as `{ "type": "json", "json_schema": { ... } }`
where `json_schema` is a JSON Schema object. The default asks for a `signals` array (each item with
`company_name`, `website`, `summary` and `sources`), plus `total_count` and `query_summary`.
Built-in Scouts carry their own fixed schema.

GlobalScout.description: A workspace Scout: what to look for, how often, and on which companies.

organizationId.description: The workspace the Scout belongs to.

name.description: The Scout's name, 1 to 200 characters.

type.description:
- `default`: a built-in Scout every workspace gets. Six exist: company announcements and press
  releases, product launches or updates, funding, M&A or financial news, executive changes or
  quotes, industry analysis mentioning the company, and controversies or negative coverage.
  They always apply to the watchlist, run daily, and can only be paused or resumed.
- `custom`: a Scout you created. Every field except the scope can be changed, and it can be deleted.

applyTo.description:
The scope, fixed at creation.
- `watchlist`: runs on every watched company, including companies watched later.
- `selected_watchlist`: runs only on the companies in `selectedCompanyIds`.
- `entire_web`: runs once across the web, not tied to a company.

selectedCompanyIds.description: The watched companies a `selected_watchlist` Scout runs on. Empty for other scopes.

category.description: A short label that groups Scouts, for example `Hiring` or `Growth & Expansion`. Signals inherit it.

queryTemplate.description:
What the Scout looks for, in plain language, up to 5,000 characters. For the `watchlist` and
`selected_watchlist` scopes, the placeholders `{{company_name}}` and `{{company_website}}` are
replaced with "the company" and "the company website", and each company's own name and website
are added to the query when it runs.

cadence.description: How often it runs. Built-in Scouts run `daily`; custom Scouts default to `weekly`.

effort.description:
Search depth for custom Scouts, `medium` by default. Each run of a custom Scout on one company
(or on the web) costs credits by effort: `low` 2.5, `medium` 7.5, `high` 10. May be absent on built-in Scouts.

isActive.description:
Whether the Scout is running. A new custom Scout is `false` until you confirm its preview.
Change it with Set a workspace Scout's state (`POST /v1/platform/global-scouts/{id}/state`).

previewStatus.description:
The preview run of a custom Scout. `pending` when created, `running` once the preview started,
`completed` when its results are in `previewData`, `failed` if it could not start or finish.
Null on built-in Scouts.

previewRunId.description: The id of the preview run. Null until a preview started.

previewData.description: The preview's findings, in the shape of `outputSchema` (by default `signals`, `total_count` and `query_summary`). Null until the preview completed.

GlobalScoutSummary.description: A workspace Scout with its signal totals across every company it runs on.

signal_counts.description: Signals found by this Scout's company Scouts.

latest_signal.description: The most recently detected signal, with `companyName` added. Null when there is none.

active_company_count.description: Companies this Scout is actively running on (active company Scouts tied to a company).

CompanyScout.description:
A workspace Scout running on one company (or, for an `entire_web` Scout, on the web). It copies its
workspace Scout's fields; change them on the workspace Scout.

baseSchemaObjectId.description: The company record it runs on. Absent for an `entire_web` Scout.

defaultScoutId.description: The workspace Scout it is a copy of.

executionMode.description: `monitor` for built-in Scouts (continuous monitoring), `task` for custom Scouts (one run per cadence period, charged in credits).

effort.description: Search depth of a custom Scout. Null on built-in Scouts.

name.description: The workspace Scout's name.

query.description: The query as it runs, with the company's name and website added.

status.description: `active` while running, `paused` while its workspace Scout is paused, `failed` when it could not run.

lastRunDate.description: When it last ran. Null before its first run.

lastRunId.description: The id of its last run.

activated_count.description: `active` only: company Scouts switched from paused (or failed) to active.

deactivated_count.description: `paused` only: company Scouts of this Scout, all now paused.

scoutSchemaId.description: The company Scout that found it (see `CompanyScout`). Its `defaultScoutId` is the workspace Scout.

baseSchemaObjectId.description: The company record the signal is about. Absent for signals of `entire_web` Scouts.

category.description: The Scout's category when the signal was found, for example `Growth & Expansion`.

scout_name.description: The Scout's name when the signal was found.

scope.description: `entire_web` for signals of web-wide Scouts, `watchlist` otherwise.

company_name.description: The company name the Scout reported. May be absent; for watched companies use `baseSchemaObjectId`.

website.description: The company's website the Scout reported, normalized to the site address. May be absent.

summary.description: What happened, in a sentence or two.

citations.description: Source URLs that support the signal.

relevance_score.description: How relevant the Scout judged the signal, 0 to 100. 0 when the Scout gave no score.

confidence_score.description: The raw score the Scout reported, either 0 to 1 or 0 to 100. Prefer `relevance_score`.

source.description: What produced the signal. Scouts write `scouts`.

detected_date.description: When the event was detected. For custom Scouts, the time of the run that found it. Lists sort on it.

status.description: `new` (unread), `read`, or `archived`. This API sets `read`; it does not archive.

raw_output.description: The Scout's structured output for this signal, in the shape of its output schema.

eventId.description: The id of the detection event. Internal; unique per run.

parallelMonitorId.description: The id of the monitor or run that produced the signal. Internal.

taskRunId.description: The id of the custom Scout run that produced the signal. Internal; absent for built-in Scouts.

webhook_timestamp.description: When the result was delivered. Internal.

SignalWithCompany.description: A signal with the name of the company it is about.

companyName.description: The company record's `company_name` (or `name`, or `Unknown`) for watched companies, otherwise the name the Scout reported. Absent when neither is known.

tasks.description: Tasks linked to a watched company.

totalActions.description: Completed background worker runs (Autonomous Updates) linked to a watched company.

totalMeetings.description: Meetings linked to a watched company.

totalDeals.description: Deal records linked to a watched company, across every deal object in the workspace.

accountStatus.description: Watched companies per value of their `account_status` field, keyed by the stored option value. Companies without a value count under `unknown`. Empty when nothing is watched.

engagementStatus.description: Watched companies per value of their `engagement_status` field, keyed by the stored option value. Companies without a value count under `unknown`. Empty when nothing is watched.

WatchedCompanyRecord.description: The company record after the change.

baseSchemaId.description: The record's object (base schema), your companies object.

data.description: The record's field values, keyed by field name (for example `company_name`, `website`, `account_status`, `engagement_status`).

isAgentAssigned.description: Whether the company is watched. `true` after watching, `false` after unwatching.

agentAssignmentStatus.description: How taking the account on is going: `STARTED` when watched, `FINISHED` once the workers have enriched it and pulled in its history, `FAILED` if that did not complete. Null after unwatching.

relationships.description: The records linked to the company.

metadata.description: Who created and last changed the record, and when.

by.description: Id of the user who created it.
Id of the user who last changed it.

KnowledgeEntry.description: A custom knowledge entry, for facts the fixed texts do not cover, such as pricing or competitors.

content.description: The entry's content, as plain text or HTML. The Heliyos app edits it as rich text.
content.example: Growth is $49 per seat per month, billed yearly. Annual contracts above 50 seats get 15% off.

KnowledgeBase.description: The knowledge base. Every text is plain text, Markdown or HTML and can be an empty string. Keys you stored that are not listed here are kept and returned as they are.

productsInformation.description: The products and services you sell.

painPoints.description: The customer problems your products solve.

qualificationCriteria.description: What makes a lead worth pursuing.

entries.description: Your team's custom entries, in display order. Can be absent when the workspace has never saved one.

WorkspaceProfile.description: The workspace's profile and knowledge base. The response also carries other workspace settings that this page does not document. Rely only on the fields listed here.

name.description: The workspace's name.

businessContext.description: What the business does, in your team's words. Empty string when not set.

website.description: The company website. Absent when not set.

industry.description: The industry. Absent when not set.

timezone.description: The workspace's time zone. Absent when not set.

address.description: Street address. Absent when not set.

state.description: State or region. Absent when not set.

zipcode.description: Postal code. Absent when not set.

logo.description: The logo, as a file id or the https URL of a file stored in Heliyos. Absent when not set.

FileLink.description: A resource the file is attached to.

objectId.description: Id of the linked record, task, interaction, or of the workspace itself for a knowledge base file.

schemaId.description: The linked record's object (base schema). Absent for links that are not records.

objectType.description: What the link points at: `company`, `people`, `deal` or a custom object's type for a record, `task`, `note`, `comment`, `interaction`, or `organization` for a knowledge base file.

id.description: The same value as `_id`. Present in list results only.

organizationId.description: The workspace the file belongs to.

fileName.description: The file's display name, as sent when the file was created.

fileSize.description: Size in bytes, as sent when the file was created.

url.description: Where the file is stored. To download the file, use Get a file download link.

storageProvider.description: The storage provider recorded when the file was created.

storageKey.description: The file's storage key, inside your workspace's folder.

description.description: An optional description. Absent when none was sent.

isKbFile.description: `true` for a knowledge base file (workers read it), `false` for a file attached to a resource.

relationships.description: The resources the file is attached to. Not hydrated.

presignedUrl.description: The signed upload URL. Send the file's bytes to it with `PUT`, within one hour. Do not send your API key to it.

fileKey.description: The storage key the file will be stored under. Send it back as `storageKey` when you create the file. Its extension comes from `mimeType`, not from `fileName`.

bucketName.description: The storage bucket the URL uploads to. You need it to build `url` when you create the file.

url.description: The link. When `forced` is `true` it is a signed link that downloads the file under its `fileName` and expires 60 seconds after the call.

forced.description: `true` for a short-lived signed download link. `false` for an older file stored outside Heliyos's upload storage: `url` is then the file's stored URL, returned as is.

_id.description: The label's id: a 24-character hexadecimal id, or `temp_` followed by digits on labels made by older versions of Heliyos.

name.description: The label's name, 1 to 100 characters, unique within its group (case-insensitive).

organizationId.description: The workspace the group belongs to.

name.description: The group's name, unique in the workspace.

description.description: What the group covers. Heliyos reads it when it classifies email threads.

isActive.description: `true` for an active group, `false` for a paused one.

color.description: The colour family the group's chip renders in, chosen by Heliyos: one of `red`, `orange`, `amber`, `olive`, `green`, `teal`, `blue`, `purple`, `pink`, `gray`. Groups created before these families existed can hold an older colour name. Absent on some older groups.

createdBy.description: Id of the user (or the API key's owner) who created the group.

TeamMembership.description: A person's membership of the workspace, or a pending invitation.

_id.description: The membership id. Present in list results.

id.description: The membership id, the same value as `_id`. Use it to remove the member or change their role.

email.description: The address the invitation was sent to, in lower case.

roleName.description: The role's name: `OWNER`, `ADMIN`, `MEMBER`, or `AGENCY` in an agency workspace. List results only.

userId.description: The person's user id. Absent while an invited person has no Heliyos account.

firstName.description: The person's first name, once they have an account. List results only.

lastName.description: The person's last name, once they have an account. List results only.

pictureUrl.description: The person's profile picture, when they set one. List results only.

status.description:
- `SENT`: invited, not joined yet. The invitation link expires 7 days after it was sent.
- `ACCEPTED`: joined by accepting an invitation.
- `REGISTERED`: joined by creating the workspace.
- `REJECTED`, `REVOKED`: found on older invitations only.

expiresOn.description: When the invitation link expires. Returned by **Invite a team member** only.

onboardingSteps.description: The person's onboarding progress in Heliyos. Empty for a new invitation. Returned by **Invite a team member** only.

name.description: The step's name.

createdAt.description: When the invitation was sent or the membership was created.

name.description:
- `OWNER`: full control, including granting and taking away the owner role.
- `ADMIN`: manages members and roles, except owners and the owner role.
- `MEMBER`: works in the workspace; cannot manage members, roles or API keys.
- `AGENCY`: the role for agency workspaces only.

type.description:
The event that notifies:
- `task.created`: a task was created.
- `task.updated`: a task changed.
- `deal.created`: a deal was created.
- `deal.updated`: a deal changed.
- `deal.approval`: a deal change is waiting for review.
- `leadset.created`: a lead set was created.
- `leadset.records.available`: new records are ready in a lead set.
- `organization.daily_summary`: the workspace's daily briefing email. Sent only when its
  frequency is `daily`.
- `scout.signal_detected`: a Scout found a signal. Always sent at once: a `daily` frequency
  is saved as `immediate`.
- `integration.not_synced`: a connected integration stopped syncing. Always sent, even when
  notifications are off or this event is not in the list (see `notifyEmails`).

frequency.description:
- `immediate`: one email per event, sent when it happens.
- `daily`: collected and sent together in the daily digest.

organizationId.description: The workspace the settings belong to.

notifyEmails.description: Every address notification emails go to. Notifications are sent only when this list has at least one address, with one exception: an `integration.not_synced` email goes to the person whose integration failed when the list is empty.

eventTypes.description: The events that send notifications, each with its frequency. An event not listed sends nothing.

isActive.description: The master switch. `false` stops every notification email except `integration.not_synced`. Events already collected for the daily digest are discarded if it is `false` when the digest goes out.

AuditMetadata.description: Who created and last changed the resource, and when.

by.description: Id of the user (or the API key's owner) who created it.
Id of the user who last changed it.

RelationshipInput.description: A link from this resource to a record (company, person, deal or custom object) or to a task or interaction in the same workspace.

objectId.description: Id of the linked record, task or interaction.

schemaId.description: Id of the linked record's object (its base schema). Recommended for records, so the link renders with the right object. Omit or send null for tasks and interactions.

objectType.description: What the link points at: `company`, `people`, `deals` or a custom object's type for records, `task` for a task, `interaction` or `meeting` for an email thread or meeting.

Relationship.description: A linked resource, hydrated with a short summary so it can be shown without another call.

schemaId.description: The linked record's object id, when the link points at a record.

data.description: A summary of the linked resource. For a record, its field values (for example `company_name` and `logo`, or `people_name`). For a task, `title` and `status`. For an interaction, `subject` and `channelType`. Empty when the target no longer exists.

schema.description: The linked record's object (`_id`, `name`, `objectType`, `fields`). Present on single-resource reads.

ListFilters.description: A JSON-encoded object, URL-encoded into the query string. See [Filtering and sorting](/api-reference/filtering). Keys: `search` (text), `filters` (array of `{ field, operator, value }`), `sort` (array of `{ field, direction }`), `page` and `pageSize` (page-number paging, `pageSize` at most 200).
